chains.title: TCF7L2 binds the ref allele at an 8q24 enhancer and may regulate MYC

links.claim: TCF7L2 binds the ref T allele more strongly than the alt C allele, but exact-base allele specificity is not established. TCF7L2 is expressed in HCT116 (63.61 TPM, rank 53/1626) and has ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks over the variant in HCT116 (E05). QBiC-SELEX gives z=-8.8 and effect=-0.429 for a CIS-BP-mapped TCF7 model, with weak k-mer sites (ref 90.0th, alt 87.2th percentile); no own TCF7L2 model is available (E20, E37). The ChIP peak is not allele-specific.
The variant lies in pELS EH38E3858447, an active enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal.

MYC is only a proximity/locus candidate: E02 places MYC 334.2 kb upstream at 8q24 and E18 gives locus biology, but there is no direct colon eQTL linking this SNP to MYC (E17, E35). L2G instead favors POU5F1B in non-colorectal credible sets with low PIP (E16).
HCT116 is a colorectal cancer line in which TCF7L2 is expressed and has an ENCODE ChIP-seq peak over this variant, so the cell context is plausible, though the peak is not allele-specific.

The colorectal cancer connection is indirect: no GWAS Catalog association for this variant, L2G credible sets are for PSA and urinary incontinence rather than colorectal cancer, and GTEx reports no significant colon eQTL. Literature supports 8q24/MYC/CCAT2/POU5F1B biology but not this specific variant-phenotype mechanism.

predictions: Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP in HCT116 should show higher ref T than alt C occupancy at this base.
If TCF7L2 regulates the enhancer, the alt C allele should produce a TCF7L2-dependent change in enhancer activity; the downstream direction depends on whether TCF7L2 activates or represses.
TCF7L2 knockdown or enhancer disruption should attenuate the allele-dependent effect.
falsified_if: Allele-specific TCF7L2 occupancy at this base in HCT116 is not higher on ref T than alt C.
TCF7L2 knockdown or enhancer disruption does not attenuate an allele-dependent enhancer or target-gene effect.
The alt C allele has no reproducible allele-specific effect in a TCF7L2-dependent assay.

chains.title: NFIC binds the alt allele strongly in vitro but lacks HCT116 occupancy evidence
chains.cell_type: HCT116 colorectal cancer cell line, with NFIC occupancy evidence currently only in HepG2

links.claim: NFIC binds the alt C allele more strongly than the ref T allele in vitro, but HCT116 occupancy is missing. E41 shows NFIC has its own QBiC-SELEX model that passes the gate strongly (z=23.35, effect=+1.226, alt>ref; strong site), and the mapped NFIB model is also strong (z=24.28, effect=+1.783). NFIC is expressed in HCT116 (36.29 TPM), but ENCODE ChIP-seq occupancy over this variant is reported only in HepG2, not HCT116 (E22, E36). NFIA shares the mapped NFIB model with identical statistics, and E39 finds no NFIA HCT116 peak, so SMAD-family occupancy in HCT116 is unsupported and NFIC versus NFIA identity remains unresolved.
The variant lies in pELS EH38E3858447, an active enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal.

POU5F1B is the best L2G gene at this locus (score 0.83) and is 79.1 kb from the variant. E40 adds a gene-level POU5F1B-colorectal cancer association, but the L2G credible sets are not colorectal cancer. E42 shows POU5F1B is not a selective dependency in HCT116 or bowel lineages, so this target-gene link remains weak and is not supported as a functional dependency. E43 finds no direct NFIC-POU5F1B colorectal cancer literature.

HCT116 expresses NFIC, but the provided ENCODE ChIP data do not show NFIC occupancy over this variant in HCT116; occupancy is only in HepG2, and E36 notes that absence could also mean no NFIC experiment in HCT116. E39 likewise finds no NFIA peak over this variant in HCT116.

POU5F1B has a gene-level colorectal cancer association in Open Targets (E40), but the credible sets containing this variant are for PSA and urinary incontinence rather than colorectal cancer, there is no colorectal cancer GWAS association for this variant, GTEx reports no significant colon eQTL, and POU5F1B is not a dependency in HCT116/bowel lineages (E42). No provided evidence ties this specific NFIC-binding allele to colorectal cancer.

predictions: If NFIC acts here, alt C should increase NFIC occupancy in HCT116 and alter POU5F1B expression in an NFIC-dependent manner.
NFIC knockdown should reduce the alt-C-dependent enhancer or POU5F1B effect.
The effect should be absent in cell types where NFIC does not occupy this element.
A TF-specific assay should distinguish NFIC from NFIA.
falsified_if: Alt C does not increase NFIC occupancy at this base in HCT116.
NFIC knockdown does not alter the alt-C-dependent enhancer or POU5F1B effect.
The effect is present where NFIC does not occupy this element.
A more specific assay fails to distinguish NFIC from NFIA and does not support NFIC over NFIA.

chains.title: SP1 binds the ref allele at the pELS and may regulate CCAT2

links.claim: SP1 binds the ref T allele more strongly than the alt C allele, but allele-specific SP1 binding is not supported. SP1 is expressed in HCT116 (38.96 TPM) and has HCT116 ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks over the variant (E06). The SP1 own QBiC-SELEX model does not pass the gate (z=-0.11, effect=-0.007); only CIS-BP-mapped SP3 (z=-7.07, effect=-0.298) and SP9 (z=-6.42, effect=-0.485) pass, both at weak k-mer sites, and mapped SP3/SP9 changes cannot substitute for SP1 (E21, E38).
The variant lies in pELS EH38E3858447, an active enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal.

CCAT2 is a positional candidate only: the variant lies in a CCAT2 non_coding_transcript_exon and the cCRE is annotated near CCAT2, but there is no direct evidence that this variant regulates CCAT2 or that SP1 mediates such regulation.
HCT116 is a colorectal cancer line in which SP1 is expressed and ChIP-bound over this variant, although the peak is not allele-specific.

The CCAT2 colorectal cancer connection is indirect in the provided literature; CCAT2 is discussed mainly in gastric/gastrointestinal cancer, and no provided genetic data link this variant to colorectal cancer through CCAT2.

predictions: Allele-specific SP1 ChIP in HCT116 should show higher ref T than alt C occupancy if M2 is correct.
If SP1 regulates CCAT2 through this enhancer, the alt C allele should alter SP1-dependent enhancer activity and CCAT2 expression.
SP1 knockdown should reduce the allele-dependent enhancer or CCAT2 effect.
falsified_if: Allele-specific SP1 occupancy at this base in HCT116 is not higher on ref T than alt C.
SP1 knockdown does not reduce an allele-dependent enhancer or CCAT2 effect.
The SP1 own QBiC-SELEX model remains non-significant and mapped SP3/SP9 effects cannot be shown to reflect SP1 binding at this base.

SP1 has HCT116 ChIP occupancy over the variant, but no SP1-specific QBiC-SELEX allelic change: the SP1 own model does not pass the gate, and mapped SP3/SP9 signals cannot establish SP1 binding direction.
E01/E03 directly annotate the variant in pELS EH38E3858447 with enhancer-like cCRE and DNase/H3K27ac signal.
CCAT2 is positional only: the variant overlaps a CCAT2 transcript and the cCRE is annotated nearby, but no cited evidence shows this variant regulates CCAT2 or that SP1 mediates it.
E06 directly shows SP1 expression in HCT116 and an HCT116 ENCODE ChIP peak over the variant, supporting cell-type plausibility, though not allele specificity.
No provided genetic or eQTL data link this variant to colorectal cancer through CCAT2; the literature connection is indirect and not variant-mechanism-specific.

NFIC has strong own-model QBiC-SELEX support for alt>ref in vitro, but HCT116 occupancy is missing; the only provided NFIC peak is in HepG2, so this is one-sided evidence and NFIC versus NFIA remains unresolved.
E01/E03 directly annotate the variant in pELS EH38E3858447 with enhancer-like cCRE and DNase/H3K27ac signal.

POU5F1B is the best L2G gene and 79.1 kb away, but the credible sets are not colorectal cancer, the gene-level association is not variant-specific, and POU5F1B is not a dependency in HCT116/bowel lineages.
HCT116 expresses NFIC, but the provided ENCODE ChIP evidence does not show NFIC occupancy over this variant in HCT116; occupancy is only in HepG2.

POU5F1B has a gene-level colorectal cancer association, but the variant-containing credible sets are for PSA and urinary incontinence, there is no colon eQTL, and no evidence ties this NFIC-binding allele to colorectal cancer.

problems: No chain has allele-specific TF occupancy or a perturbation/reporter assay at this base; all TF binding claims remain inference from ChIP peaks plus in vitro QBiC-SELEX.
M1.binding relies on a CIS-BP-mapped TCF7 model rather than an own TCF7L2 model, and the QBiC site is weak; the HCT116 ChIP peak is not allele-specific.
M2.binding lacks an SP1-specific QBiC-SELEX change: the SP1 own model does not pass the gate, while mapped SP3/SP9 models cannot establish SP1 binding at this base.
M3.binding has strong in vitro NFIC QBiC-SELEX support for alt>ref, but no HCT116 occupancy; the only provided NFIC peak is in HepG2, and NFIC versus NFIA remains unresolved.
M1.gene and M2.gene are positional only; MYC and CCAT2 are not shown to be regulated by this variant in colon/HCT116, and no colon eQTL supports either link.

M3.gene uses POU5F1B L2G scores from PSA and urinary-incontinence credible sets, not colorectal cancer; gene-level Open Targets association and lack of dependency do not establish a variant-to-POU5F1B mechanism.
All phenotype links are weak: no GWAS Catalog association for this variant, no significant colon GTEx eQTL, and the literature is locus/gene-level rather than variant-mechanism-specific.
The null chain M4 remains favored over M1-M3, but M3 retains the strongest in vitro binding signal despite missing HCT116 occupancy.

critic_checks.why: Confirms whether TCF7L2 has an own QBiC-SELEX model or only CIS-BP-mapped models, which could upgrade or downgrade the TCF7L2 binding link.
Tests the missing HCT116 occupancy evidence for NFIC over this variant; a positive HCT116 peak would strengthen M3.binding, while confirmed absence keeps it weak.
Helps resolve NFIC versus NFIA identity at the shared NFIB-mapped motif; NFIA occupancy in HCT116 could weaken the NFIC-specific claim.
